name: Black Hole with Skyrmion Hair
description: A static spherical black hole surrounded by a self-gravitating Skyrme field, with a fractional baryon number outside its horizon.
convention: We use $c=1$ and keep $G$ explicit. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu}=R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: A horizon cuts through a skyrmion, leaving part of its field outside. The field has energy and curves the space around the hole. For a static, spherically symmetric solution, $ds^2=-N(r)^2C(r)dt^2+dr^2/C(r)+r^2d\Omega^2$, with $C(r)=1-2Gm(r)/r$ and $c=1$ [shiiki2005skyrme]. The horizon lies where $C(r_h)=0$, and the functions approach $N=1$ and $m=M$ far away [dvali2016skyrmion].¶A skyrmion is a localized configuration of a nonlinear field used to model a baryon. In the spherical configuration the field points radially in its internal space, with an angle $f(r)$ that falls to zero at infinity [shiiki2005skyrme]. If its value at the horizon is $f_h$, the baryon number outside the horizon is $B_{\rm out}=(2f_h-\sin 2f_h)/(2\pi)$ [shiiki2005skyrme]. For $0<f_h<\pi$, the baryon number outside the horizon is fractional [shiiki2005skyrme].¶Hugh Luckock and Ian Moss studied a skyrmion around a Schwarzschild black hole in 1986 [shiiki2005skyrme, luckock1986]. The Schwarzschild geometry in their calculation has a fixed mass, while the skyrmion field occupies the exterior [shiiki2005skyrme, dvali2016skyrmion]. Serge Droz, Markus Heusler, and Norbert Straumann included the gravity of the field and found static black holes with Skyrme hair numerically in 1991 [dvali2016skyrmion, droz1991]. Their solutions approach Schwarzschild's geometry far from the hole [droz1991].¶The field and the geometry obey coupled equations, and the values at the horizon are chosen to meet the conditions at infinity [shiiki2005skyrme]. Two solutions can share the same horizon radius and coupling constants while carrying different field profiles [dvali2016skyrmion]. A linear stability analysis distinguishes a branch stable against spherical perturbations from another with an unstable mode [shiiki2005skyrme, dvali2016skyrmion].¶The massless pion model has a dimensionless coupling $\alpha=4\pi G F_\pi^2$, where $F_\pi$ is the pion decay constant [shiiki2005skyrme]. For a fixed coupling, skyrmion black holes have been found up to a maximum horizon radius [dvali2016skyrmion]. As the horizon radius shrinks to zero, the solutions approach gravitating skyrmions [shiiki2005skyrme]. Far from the horizon the profile falls as $1/r^2$ [dvali2016skyrmion].

related.text: The vacuum black hole approached far from the skyrmion, with the same total mass [dvali2016skyrmion].
A spherical black hole with a scalar field coupled to its electromagnetic field [horowitz1992, garfinkle1991].
A spherical Yang-Mills field held together by its gravity, with a regular centre [volkov1999, bartnik1988].

parameters.description: Dimensionless lapse, normalized to $N\to 1$ far away. In $x=aF_\pi r$, its equation is $N_x/N=(\alpha/4)(x+8\sin^2 f/x)f_x^2$.
Dimensionless radial function, $C=1-2Gm(r)/r$, with $C(r_h)=0$ and $C>0$ outside the horizon.
Mass function approaching $M$ at infinity. In $x=aF_\pi r$, $\mu=aF_\pi Gm$ obeys $\mu_x=(\alpha/8)[C(x^2+8\sin^2 f)f_x^2+2\sin^2 f+4\sin^4 f/x^2]$.
Dimensionless Skyrme profile, with $f(\infty)=0$ and $f(r_h)=f_h$. With $u=x^2+8\sin^2 f$, it obeys $(NCu f_x)_x=N\sin(2f)(1+4Cf_x^2+4\sin^2 f/x^2)$, where $x=aF_\pi r$.
Areal radius of the event horizon.
Pion decay constant of the Skyrme model.
Dimensionless Skyrme coupling; $x=aF_\pi r$ is the dimensionless radius.
